topic_summary: Analysis of the Renaissance humanist reconstruction of Classical Latin as a contested kernel. Medieval users read 'correct Latin' as a living drifted vernacular continuous with Classical forms. Humanist reconstructors read it as the Classical form recovered from texts, requiring discontinuous return to a fixed reference point with no living practitioners as intermediaries.

key_entities: Medieval Latin users (practitioners of drifted vernacular claiming continuity)
Humanist reconstructors (Petrarch, Valla, Erasmus - textual archaeologists)
Classical Latin corpus (Cicero, Virgil, Caesar - the stabilized kernel)
Medieval Latin texts (legal, ecclesiastical, scholastic - the drifted form)
Renaissance printing press (mechanism for kernel stabilization and distribution)
key_tensions: Continuity vs discontinuity (living tradition vs archaeological recovery)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Classical Latin as codified in the literary corpus of Cicero, Virgil, Caesar, and other canonical authors - a fixed linguistic reference point claimed as the legitimate standard
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between practice-based legitimacy (medieval users claiming unbroken transmission) and textual-archaeological legitimacy (humanists claiming direct access to original forms via philological reconstruction)

readings.commitment: Correct Latin is the living form transmitted through unbroken practice, incorporating natural linguistic drift as legitimate development
readings.authority_grounding: Practice-norm: legitimacy derives from continuous institutional use (Church, law, university) - the living speakers ARE the authority
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low suppression of alternatives (drift is legitimate); beneficiary is existing institutional users; victim set is empty or minimal (only 'barbarisms' excluded); extractiveness moderate (gatekeeping via institutional access but no systematic delegitimization of practice)

readings.commitment: Correct Latin is the Classical form recoverable only through philological archaeology, requiring discontinuous return to textual sources and rejection of medieval drift
readings.authority_grounding: Textual-archaeological: legitimacy derives from demonstrated fidelity to the stabilized corpus - the texts ARE the authority, not living practice
readings.expected_structural_delta: High suppression of alternatives (medieval forms delegitimized as 'corruption'); beneficiary is humanist elite with philological training; victim set is existing institutional users whose Latin is now 'incorrect'; extractiveness high (systematic delegitimization of practice-based authority, creation of new gatekeeping class)

readings.commitment: Correct Latin requires both textual fidelity to Classical norms AND recognition of legitimate post-Classical developments in technical/ecclesiastical domains
readings.authority_grounding: Dual: textual authority for literary/rhetorical forms, practice authority for specialized institutional vocabularies
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate suppression (some medieval forms legitimized, others rejected); beneficiary is institutional users who adopt Classical norms while retaining domain-specific vocabulary; victim set is reduced (only 'barbarisms' excluded, not all drift); extractiveness moderate (partial delegitimization but with accommodation)

axes.structural_delta: Latin as living language with legitimate drift through continuous institutional practice
axes.primary_observable: Acceptance of post-Classical vocabulary and syntax in authoritative texts; institutional resistance to humanist reforms
axes.selection_reason: First reading: establishes baseline of practice-based authority before reconstruction challenge

axes.structural_delta: Latin as dead language requiring discontinuous philological recovery from fixed textual corpus
axes.primary_observable: Systematic rejection of medieval forms; creation of new grammatical/lexical standards based on Classical corpus analysis; humanist educational curricula
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: highest centrality; establishes the extractive dimension of reconstruction as delegitimization

axes.structural_delta: Dual authority structure: Classical norms for rhetoric/literature, practice norms for technical domains
axes.primary_observable: Retention of medieval legal/theological terminology alongside Classical literary standards; Erasmus's ecclesiastical Latin reforms
axes.selection_reason: Third reading: synthesis node showing how the kernel contest resolved in practice through partial accommodation

axes.human_readable: Printing Press as Kernel Stabilization Mechanism
axes.structural_delta: Mechanical reproduction technology enabling mass distribution of standardized Classical texts and grammars
axes.primary_observable: Publication rates of Classical editions vs medieval texts; standardization of orthography and grammar across printed works
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: mountain providing technological constraint but lower structural distinctiveness than the three readings themselves

axes.structural_delta: Reconstructed Classical Latin as mechanism for excluding vernacular speakers from elite discourse
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between Classical Latin mastery and access to university/ecclesiastical/diplomatic positions; resistance to vernacular translation
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: captured indirectly via reconstruction_reading's victim structure; additional axis would over-split the beneficiary analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Mechanical reproduction enabling mass distribution of standardized texts
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Mountain providing technological constraint but lower structural distinctiveness than the kernel readings; technological enabler rather than interpretive commitment

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Reconstructed Latin as barrier excluding vernacular speakers from elite discourse
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Extractive dimension captured via reconstruction_reading's victim structure; separate axis would over-split beneficiary analysis without adding structural novelty

omegas.description: Was the reconstruction a D1 break (discontinuous reoccupation of symbol from external reference) or D2 (continuous evolution with retrospective legitimation)? If D1, the 'same Latin' claim is false - humanists created a new language using the old name. If D2, continuity reading has stronger structural validity.
omegas.source: User's kernel contest framing + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

omegas.description: Was the Classical corpus genuinely accessible as a fixed reference, or did humanists construct 'Classical Latin' through selective reading and normalization? If constructed, the kernel itself is a reading, not a stable substrate.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - no entity for 'Classical Latin as actually practiced' vs 'Classical Latin as textually preserved'

omegas.description: Why did ecclesiastical Latin survive reconstruction pressure when legal/scholastic Latin did not? Hybrid reading suggests domain-specific resistance, but mechanism unclear. Possible mountain of liturgical fixity vs rope of legal adaptability.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) - Church as institution with power to resist humanist authority claims

omegas.description: If humanist reconstruction had failed, would vernaculars have displaced Latin earlier? Reconstruction may have extended Latin's elite status by making it 'pure' rather than 'corrupt', delaying vernacular ascendancy.
omegas.source: Deferred axis vernacular_displacement + absence of vernacular-Latin competition mechanism in extraction

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel contest confirmed: three readings emit structurally distinct constraints (different victim sets, different extractiveness levels, different authority grounding). Continuity reading treats drift as legitimate (low suppression); reconstruction reading treats drift as corruption (high suppression, new gatekeeping class); hybrid reading splits authority by domain (moderate suppression, partial accommodation). The D1/D2 break question remains omega-bounded but does not prevent constraint generation.
